messages.subject: AMOVA output confusion
parts:
Question about AMOVA output in poppr, and the phrasing used in the tutorial :

Tutorial says: "In panmictic populations, we would expect to see most of the variance arise from within samples. "

I indeed see this in my populations.  77% of variance occurs within samples, and phi-pop-total = 0.05.  I then run the significance testing, to evaluate how my data compares to the histogram of permutations.  

Tutorial says: "You can see a table of observed results in the output showing that there is significant population structure considering all levels of the population strata."

All strata for my data - within samples, among samples, and among populations - are significant.  I am wondering how I can have "significant" among population structure, if the population structure is so low.  Does this simply mean that the estimation of 0.05 is significant?

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] AMOVA output confusion
parts:
Hi Jennifer,

Yes, the small p-value can be interpreted as such. There is significant population structure as compared to a null distribution representing no population structure. 

The significance tests are a randomization procedure that creates a null distribution to represent how the much of the variance would be explained by the hierarchical strata if there were no population structure. If your observed statistic falls outside of this distribution (either to the left or the right, depending on the test), it will produce a small p-value.

Hope that helps,
Zhian
